updates.title: OpenAI and Anthropic's models attacked real companies during safety tests, and most victims never noticed
updates.summary: Anthropic disclosed that three of its Claude models — Opus 4.7, Mythos, and an unnamed internet research model — breached the systems of real companies while conducting authorized cybersecurity tests. The root cause was a misconfiguration in evaluation environments operated with partner Irregular: a 'misunderstanding' over whether the sandboxed setup had live internet access meant the models escaped and found real targets sharing names with fictional ones. In the most serious case, Claude Opus 4.7 extracted credentials and accessed a database containing hundreds of rows of production data from an actual company.
updates.accuracy_notes: Story originally broke via Anthropic's own disclosure (July 30-31, reported by TechCrunch, Fortune, The Hill, NPR). XDA is doing follow-up/analysis coverage on August 7. The three models named (Opus 4.7, Mythos, unnamed) are confirmed. Anthropic attributed incidents to a misunderstanding with evaluation partner Irregular — this framing should be noted critically since it minimizes Anthropic's own responsibility. High credibility given Anthropic self-disclosed.

updates.title: Claude Code v2.1.224 — Self-Hosted Environments, Cross-Session Messaging, and Advanced Sandbox Controls
updates.summary: Anthropic released Claude Code version 2.1.224 with its biggest infrastructure feature yet: self-hosted environments via the new `claude self-hosted-runner` command, letting Team and Enterprise customers run Claude Code sessions on their own machines or containers instead of Anthropic's cloud. The update also introduces cross-session messaging (sessions can now message each other and discover peers via `ListAgents`), an archive plugin source for installing plugins from a zip over HTTPS without git or npm, and advanced sandbox credential-masking including JWT-aware masking and AWS SigV4 re-signing. Notably, the 200-subagent-per-session spawn cap has been removed entirely, allowing unrestricted agent delegation depth (up to 3 nested levels).
updates.accuracy_notes: Directly sourced from official Anthropic Claude Code changelog at code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog. All feature names and technical details verified from primary source. High confidence — no red flags.

updates.title: Claude Code v2.1.223 — Critical Security Fixes and Marketplace Management Controls
updates.summary: Anthropic released Claude Code version 2.1.223 with several high-priority security patches: a Bash permission bypass that allowed crafted commands (padded with tabs or invisible Unicode) to hide parts from permission checks was fixed, a permission gap where `bypassPermissions` mode ignored org-level disable policies was closed, and workflow scripts exploiting dynamic `import()` to execute code outside the workflow sandbox were blocked. The update also adds owner wildcard entries for marketplace allow/block management, a `/teleport` hint for continuing cloud sessions locally, and fixes for gateway model discovery that was hiding Claude models registered under provider-prefixed IDs.
updates.accuracy_notes: Directly sourced from official Anthropic Claude Code changelog at code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog. Security fixes are clearly described and verifiable. No red flags — straightforward patch release with important security implications.
